clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient, a girl detected in infancy with bilateral polycystic kidneys and a left flank palpable mass, had no family history of cystic kidney disease. Clinical progression included characteristic TSC skin lesions (facial angiofibromas and hypopigmented macules) documented at 10 years, and renal angiomyolipomas detected on ultrasound. Neurological assessment by brain MRI at 13 years revealed multiple cortical tubers and calcified subependymal nodules, consistent with tuberous sclerosis complex involvement. Kidney function remained normal throughout early follow-up. Genetic testing confirming TSC2/PKD1 contiguous gene deletion was ordered but the direct genetic report was not available in the disclosed evidence.
